opponent: SLOT: “WE FELL IN THAT TRAP WITH BOTH GOALS!”  Man Utd
speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Hey Arne, what was your verdict on that and what  did you say at half time after that first half? 
That wasn’t necessary to be two nil down.  It wasn’t necessary to lose this game today,  
although United deserved to be two nil  up. Let that be completely clear. But  
we conceded two goals and they have a lot of  strength. Let that also be clear. But two of  
them are definitely the set piece and the counter  attack, and we fell in that trap with both goals.  
So the first one we concede from a set piece,  and the second one we played through the middle,  
where their players are sharp in the duels, and a  great counter attack led to the two nil. I did see  
us in the first half coming into good positions,  but that did not lead to anything. A few shots,  
but nothing serious. And I said if we can combine  coming into these positions with a bit more intent  
in arriving in the box, that’s why I changed and  brought Cody in, or not brought him in, but put  
him in a number nine position. And then we are  able to do more than only having ball possession.  
And that’s what happened in the second half also,  of course, because we immediately found the goal  
because they misplaced the pass. Great finish by  Dominik, but they misplaced the pass, and then  
you have your momentum on your side. And that’s  what we had in the second half, I think, changed. 
Pierce, why do you think your team  did start so bad? Was it a tactical  
problem or a mentality problem? You mean we conceded two goals? 
Well, just, you lost everything, didn’t  you, in the first 15, 20 minutes? 
Yeah, we lost a lot. That is true. Yeah, yeah.  And indeed also, you know when you come here that  
they want to start strong and aggressive, and  we were aware of that. But as you said, I think  
we were. But when did we concede the first goal?  Was that after six minutes? Six minutes now? Maybe  
that’s the answer then. Indeed, in this first six  minutes, I saw us not picking up the second balls,  
although we had a few moments where we pressed  them high. But if you concede after six minutes  
in this stadium, then you always know you’re going  to face a struggle period afterwards. And I think  
after us conceding the goal, we controlled the  ball. Having the ball, we didn’t control the ball,  
we controlled ball possession, controlled the game  by ball possession. But yeah, then I think it was  
one of the first times after we lost the ball  and they counter attacked us to 2-0. And then  
of course everything you’ve done before deserves  a lot of criticism. But I don’t think there was  
that much difference between the first and the  second half. The only difference there was that we  
were better able to control their counter attacks  and create more from the ball possession we had. 
Do you think the second goal  should have been ruled out? 
Yeah, yeah. If it was a touch, which I think it  is, because if you know a bit about a ball sport,  
you know that if a ball has a certain curve and  the curve changes, there must have been contact,  
but it’s always light. Yeah. Then we should have  a debate in football. Is that then enough to  
disallow a goal? But I think the rule is, if there  was a touch, it should have been disallowed. But  
I don’t think it’s a surprise to anyone this  season that if there is a VAR intervention,  
or if there’s something that you could  look at, or could be left, could be right,  
that decision goes against us. That has been the  whole season, every single time the same. So if I  
remember Paris Saint-Germain at home getting  a penalty for a soft touch on Mac Allister,  
but of course the VAR interferes and says, no,  no, this is not a penalty. Where one week later,  
when I see Paris Saint-Germain playing against  Bayern Munich, that same soft touch, the penalty  
stays. I saw last week my goalkeeper on the  floor with an injury and the referee doesn’t  
stop the game. I see a player of United off the  pitch today and the referee stops the game when  
we try to play on. That has been our whole season.  But the second goal we did not concede because of  
that handball. We conceded it because we lost the  ball in a stupid position and we lost a few big  
moments afterwards in duels. So we have to first  look at ourselves. Let that be completely clear  
and obvious. But that decisions have gone every  single game against us, that’s also completely  
clear and obvious, because when we played United  in the first game of the season, I had one of my  
players with five stitches on the floor and the  referee didn’t stop the game and we conceded. This  
is a complete pattern over the whole season. But  there’s also a pattern that we concede ridiculous  
goals when we are the better team. That one or  two switching off and then we concede a goal,  
and that is something we have more influence  on. So I should focus much more on that than on  
these referee decisions that go against us. But  it’s clear that it’s the whole season the same. 
I mean, you obviously were out without  Salah and you were without Ekitike and  
then Isak. What is the situation with Alex? Is  he going to be out for the rest of the season? 
No, he isn’t. No, he isn’t. No. We’re  expecting him to be back very soon. But  
you saw the second half, so there’s no  excuse. I haven’t spoken about missing  
players. I’m not talking about it now.  If you can play a second half as we did,  
there’s no necessity to have other players here.  We were able with this team to have a chance of  
winning this game and we were quite close. But as  always, one moment of switching off immediately  
leads to us conceding a goal when there was a  moment where it was, and I think the Liverpool  
journalists recognise this so many times this  season, it was waiting for us to score one  
and then we conceded because we switched off  for one or two seconds in a crucial moment. 
You’re still maybe three points away  from confirming the Champions League  
spot. Are you concerned that you haven’t  quite done it yet? Because there’s a six  
point gap between yourself and Paul, but  still, you still have to do it, I guess. 
Yeah. I wouldn’t say concerned is the right word,  but I’m completely aware of the fact that we need  
three points. That’s why I was so annoyed that  we didn’t pick them up today. Although we didn’t  
deserve to get these points in the first half,  let’s be completely clear. But if you are 2-2,  
coming back after 2-0 down, then you  should at least go away here with a result,  
which we didn’t do. And we knew before the  game we had four chances to pick up three  
points to qualify for Champions League, and  now there are three chances left. Thank you.
